body.statement: Given a terminating saturation system satisfying the ranked fixing-overlap handle, Global-CID terminates on every feasible encoded input and returns exactly one of two checkable objects. A formula return is a guarded circuit \(F\) whose overlap common-value condition makes \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,P_M)\) total and satisfies \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,P_M)(c_y;c_x)=Q_M(c_y;c_x)\) simultaneously for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,d)\) and every \((c_x,c_y)\). A negative return is a bounded collision certificate. The algorithm returns a circuit if and only if the macro target is uniformly identified. If the supplied saturation additionally has state count, transition cost, and terminal encoding length within the quantitative objective of the overlap-normal-form question, then the total bit complexity and encoded output length are at most \(B_{\mathrm{out}}(\ell)\).
body.justification: The formula-or-collision dichotomy gives arbitrary clustering the same constructive identification standard that ordinary ID provides for one known ADMG.
body.gap: AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG proves ID completeness only for acyclic cluster diagrams, and FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG Theorem 4 is rulewise completeness that its conclusion says does not compare different rule sequences or prove a complete nonidentification characterization.
body.consumer: Anand and Hripcsak's ALARM grouping can receive either one implementable effect functional or two explicit micro-level mechanisms showing why the chosen clinical clustering is insufficient.
